subject: Aurum Health: latency spike + hallucination increase after qprofile v2 rollout
messages:
From: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@aurumhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden P99 latency spike + hallucination rate after model update

Mina / Stephanie —

We pushed your qprofile v2 on our dedicated pool last night (per the change window). Since the rollout we've observed: 
- 3x increase in P99 latency (from ~520ms to ~1.6s) for our clinical-NER route
- A rise in hallucination-style token replacements in ~2.3% of responses (samples attached)
- Error rate (5xx) went from 0.05% to 0.9% during peak at 08:00 PST this morning

This is causing delays for downstream ingestion and manual triage load for our clinicians. We rolled back to qprofile v1 at 07:30 and saw latency improve, but we need root cause and a plan to prevent a recurrence. Can we get an executive summary and ETA for a mitigation?

Attachments: perf_dump_0629.csv, error_samples_0629.txt

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Engineering Manager, Aurum Health
ops+oncall@aurumhealth.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency spike + hallucination rate after model update

Daniel — thanks for the quick heads-up and for attaching the dumps. I'm sorry you hit this. We're treating it as high priority and have looped in Eng + Product.

Immediate plan: 
- Markus and Rishi will triage the runtime traces and qprofile diff (see qprofile-v2-diff.txt).
- Stephanie will coordinate a short postmortem call and work with you on the customer-facing summary.
- I will escalate to ops leadership if we confirm qprofile v2 is the root cause.

Can you confirm the exact hosts/pool ids you used for the v2 rollout and whether any other config changes coincided with the window? Also, can you share the HubSpot deal id so we can reflect severity on the account?

Mina
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
(attachment: qprofile-v2-diff.txt)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency spike + hallucination rate after model update

Thanks — preliminary findings from a quick dive: 
- The qprofile v2 introduces a new int8 path that increases kernel fusion for KV-cache rows. On longer context lengths (800+ tokens), we see serialization points causing thread stalls on our CUDA queue on T4s. That matches the P99 spike.
- The hallucination samples look like token-decoding mismatches when mixed-precision paths hit a fallback in the sampling stage. Not present with v1.
- The 5xxs correlate with OOM-protection retries when the fused kernel runs out of workspace; the runtime retries and sometimes returns a 5xx on the client side.

Immediate mitigations I propose: 
1) Disable the new int8 kernel for Aurum's dedicated pool (hotfix) — restores v1-like path.
2) Add a runtime guard to force lower batch sizes when context > 512 for qprofile v2.
3) Collect a focused perf trace under synthetic load to reproduce the stall and confirm the workspace calculation bug.

I can deploy the hotfix to the Aurum pool in a 30-minute change if Mina approves. We should capture the perf trace before full rollback if possible.

-Markus
VP, Serving Runtime

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency spike + hallucination rate after model update

Markus — please proceed with the hotfix disable for Aurum's pool now. Rishi, pair with Markus on the perf trace; leave the diagnostic trace running for 20 minutes and capture both kernel logs and sampling path logs.

Stephanie — set a 1pm PST postmortem call with Aurum and include a short exec brief for our internal leadership (one-pager: impact, root cause hypothesis, short-term fix, long-term action items). I'll need the brief by 12:30.

Lauren — start a risk review for the qprofile rollout plan; we need stricter compatibility checks for mixed-precision and context-length distributions.

Mina

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@aurumhealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 14:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 latency spike + hallucination rate after model update — postmortem invite + materials

Daniel — thank you again for your patience. We completed the hotfix rollout to your dedicated pool at 10:45 PST on 6/29, which reverted the int8 fused kernel path for qprofile v2. Observed improvement: P99 returned to baseline within 20 minutes.

Attachments: perf_dump_0629.csv (annotated), error_samples_0629.txt, internal_exec_brief_v1.pdf (attachment stub)

Agenda for 1pm PST postmortem: 
- 1) Timeline and what we observed (5m)
- 2) Engineering root cause (Markus) (10m)
- 3) Short-term mitigations completed (hotfix, runtime guard) (10m)
- 4) Customer impact and credit request (Daniel) (5m)
- 5) Action items and rollout policy changes (Lauren/Mina) (15m)

Next steps (action items): 
- Markus + Rishi: root cause PR with repro and unit test by 7/2 EOD.
- Lauren: updated rollout checklist (including context-length gating) by 7/6.
- Mina + Stephanie: customer-facing summary + credit recommendation by 7/1.

See you on the call — invite sent.

-Stephanie
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
